raw_case_text:
A 72-year-old man, residing in Eastern France (Alsace), was admitted to the medical intensive care unit in October 2012 for acute calculous cholecystitis associated with severe sepsis. No liver abscess was diagnosed at that time. He had a history of suspected amebic liver abscess, operated and treated by metronidazole, after a trip to Senegal in 1985. The last time the patient traveled to endemic areas dates back to 1990, i.e. the West Indies. In November 2012, a few days after his release from the hospital, the patient consulted again for abdominal pain in the right upper quadrant with an inflammatory syndrome (C-reactive protein: 237 mg/L, procalcitonin: 71.2 ng/mL) without fever. Abdominal CT scan revealed a liver abscess. A liver puncture sample sent to the bacteriology laboratory was sterile. No parasitological sampling was conducted. A broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment by vancomycin (2 g/day), Tazocin (piperacillin/tazobactam) (12 g/day), and metronidazole (1500 mg/day) was implemented for a period of 3 weeks. Treatment with metronidazole was not continued by the patient due to poor digestive tolerance.
In December 2012, the patient was again hospitalized in the nephrology department for acute renal failure probably related to drug toxicity due to trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (creatinine: 360.4 mumol/L, urea: 14.3 mmol/L, Glomerular Filtration Rate: 15 ml/min/1.73 m2).
At this time, the patient presented no biological inflammatory syndrome (CRP: 7.6 mg/L) or liver anomalies (ASAT: 19 U/L, ALAT: 13 U/L, gammaGT: 47 U/L, PAL: 154 U/L, total bilirubin: 7.4 mumol/L, conjugated bilirubin: 3.6 mumol/L) and was apyretic. MR cholangiopancreatography revealed a partitioned collection fluid (6.6 cm x 4 cm) in segments I and II, and an abscess in segment VII (5.5 cm x 5 cm) (Figs. 1-3).
Hydatid disease and alveolar echinococcosis serologies (these larval cestodes being endemic in Eastern France) were negative. However, amebiasis serology by ELISA Ridascreen E. histolytica IgG, (R-Biopharm GmbH, Darmstadt, Germany) was positive (IgG: 8.72; threshold: 0.9), as was latex agglutination (Bichro-Latex Amibe Fumouze, Fumouze Diagnostics, Levallois-Perret, France). In-house Entamoeba histolytica PCR was performed on a puncture of the liver abscess. DNA was extracted from 200 muL of the sample using the QIAamp DNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Courtaboeuf, France). PCR amplification was carried out as described by Gonin and Trudel using HotStarTaq DNA Polymerase PCR Buffer 1X (Qiagen), 1 U HotStarTaq DNA Polymerase (Qiagen), 200 muM dNTPs, 1 mM MgCl2, and 0.5 muM of each primer ED1 + EDH2 for the detection of Entamoeba dispar or EH1 + EDH2 for the detection of Entamoeba histolytica. Cycling conditions were as follows: 15 min incubation at 95  C followed by 40 cycles consisting of 30 s at 95  C, 60 s at 51  C, and 40 s at 72  C, with a final 5 min elongation at 72  C. The PCR was monitored by positive and negative controls. This in-house PCR test was positive, thus confirming the diagnosis of ALA.
Direct examination by microscopy and culture of the aspirated liver abscess fluid were negative. The stool examination performed in this patient in January 2013 was also negative. The clinical course was favorable after 14 days of metronidazole and 10 days of tiliquinol-tilbroquinol.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 72-year-old French man presented with right upper quadrant abdominal pain one month after hospitalization for acute calculous cholecystitis, followed a month later by acute renal failure and persistent hepatic abscesses.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In October 2012, the patient was hospitalized in the ICU for acute calculous cholecystitis with severe sepsis (no liver abscess seen at that time). Days after discharge in November 2012, he re-presented with afebrile right upper quadrant abdominal pain and marked systemic inflammation; a liver abscess was found on CT (sterile on bacterial culture) and treated with 3 weeks of IV vancomycin, piperacillin/tazobactam, and poorly tolerated metronidazole. In December 2012, he was readmitted with trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole-induced acute kidney injury and persistent hepatic collections.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of an operated and metronidazole-treated amebic liver abscess in 1985 following travel to Senegal; last travel to an endemic area (West Indies) was in 1990; resided in Alsace, Eastern France.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for right upper quadrant pain and metronidazole gastrointestinal intolerance; negative for fever at readmission.

objective.physical_examination: Afebrile on readmission in November and December 2012 with right upper quadrant abdominal pain.
objective.routine_investigations: In November 2012, labs showed CRP 237 mg/L and procalcitonin 71.2 ng/mL. In December 2012, labs showed acute renal failure (creatinine 360.4 umol/L, urea 14.3 mmol/L, eGFR 15 mL/min/1.73 m2), CRP 7.6 mg/L, AST 19 U/L, ALT 13 U/L, GGT 47 U/L, ALP 154 U/L, total bilirubin 7.4 umol/L, and conjugated bilirubin 3.6 umol/L. Stool microscopy (Jan 2013) was negative. Serologies for Echinococcus granulosus and Echinococcus multilocularis were negative, whereas Entamoeba histolytica IgG ELISA (index 8.72; threshold 0.9) and Bichro-Latex Amibe agglutination were strongly positive.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial November 2012 abdominal CT showed a liver abscess with sterile bacterial aspirate. December 2012 MRCP revealed a 6.6 x 4 cm partitioned fluid collection in hepatic segments I and II and a 5.5 x 5 cm abscess in segment VII. In-house PCR on aspirated liver abscess pus was positive for Entamoeba histolytica (microscopy and bacterial culture of the aspirate were negative).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Late-relapsing or recurrent amebic liver abscess (27 years after initial Senegal travel) confirmed by positive Entamoeba histolytica serology (ELISA and latex agglutination) and positive abscess fluid E. histolytica PCR, with cystic and alveolar echinococcosis ruled out by negative serologies. The patient achieved a favorable clinical and radiological recovery following 14 days of metronidazole followed by 10 days of intraluminal tiliquinol-tilbroquinol.
